red_flags: Systolic BP >= 180 and/or diastolic BP >= 120 mmHg WITH symptoms of target-organ damage
Visual disturbance, dizziness, confusion or headache in this context
Breathlessness, worse when lying down, or leg swelling in this context
Sudden weakness, speech or swallowing difficulty, or vision problems in this context
first_line: Measure blood pressure accurately at every clinic visit for adults aged 18 years and above
Confirm hypertension using readings from two different clinic visits, except when systolic BP >= 160 and/or diastolic BP >= 100 mmHg, where one clinic visit is sufficient under this STW
Advise lifestyle modification, including limiting salt intake to less than 5 g/day and 30 minutes of daily physical activity
Use the ICMR pharmacotherapy protocols according to the patient's clinical circumstances
referral_criteria: BP >= 180 systolic and/or >= 120 diastolic with symptoms of target-organ damage: stabilise ABC and refer to emergency care at a higher centre
For severe BP elevation without signs of acute target-organ damage, follow the STW management protocol and refer/admit if symptoms or organ damage are suspected
level_of_care: Primary care assessment with emergency referral to a higher centre when indicated

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow: Hypertension in Adults

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Systolic BP 90 mmHg, heart rate >150 or <50/min
Congestive heart failure (CHF), transient ischemic attack (TIA) or stroke
Major bleeding while on oral anticoagulants
first_line: Detailed clinical evaluation
Basic investigations and careful ECG evaluation
Categorize atrial fibrillation
Assess stroke risk and need for anticoagulation
Assess bleeding risk
At PHC/CHC, the workflow specifies starting oral anticoagulation
The workflow specifies rate-control medication when heart rate is >110/min and there is no evidence of CHF
referral_criteria: Refer from PHC/CHC if indicators for early intervention are present
At district hospital, refer if heart rate remains uncontrolled, or CHF or angina is present
level_of_care: Initial evaluation and management at PHC/CHC, escalation to district hospital and tertiary centre as indicated

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Atrial Fibrillation

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

first_line: Monitor urine volume and body weight
Identify and treat life-threatening complications
Correct hydration status
Stop nephrotoxic drugs
Exclude urinary outlet obstruction
Stabilize blood pressure
Treat infection
Assess need for dialysis
referral_criteria: Indications for dialysis
Unexplained AKI
Involvement of other organs
Sepsis
Systemic disease
Complicated pregnancy
level_of_care: Primary, secondary and tertiary care, with timely referral after stabilisation

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for the Management of Acute Kidney Injury

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Orbital involvement: periorbital edema, erythema, displaced globe, ophthalmoplegia or visual disturbance
Non-resolution with oral antibiotics for ten days
Facial hypoesthesia or facial, palatal or turbinate discoloration suggesting invasive fungal sinusitis
first_line: Oral antibiotics as specified in the workflow for 7–10 days
Topical budesonide or mometasone nasal spray
Normal saline nasal washes
Adequate hydration and steam inhalation
Topical or oral decongestants for 3–5 days
Antihistamines for patients with co-existing allergy
investigations: Endoscopy-guided nasal swabs or KOH smear in non-resolving or worsening cases
CT PNS for suspected complications or non-resolving cases
referral_criteria: Orbital or intracranial complications
Non-resolution after at least 7 days of oral antibiotics
Worsening symptoms during oral antibiotic treatment
Suspected invasive fungal sinusitis
level_of_care: PHC/primary level, district hospital and tertiary care depending on complications

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow for the Management of Acute Rhinosinusitis

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Osmotic symptoms: polyuria, polydipsia and polyphagia
first_line: Dietary modification
Avoidance of tobacco and restriction or avoidance of alcohol
Physical activity
Pharmacotherapy according to HbA1c and the workflow
Follow up to meet metabolic targets
investigations: Urine routine examination and spot albumin-creatinine ratio
Liver function tests: ALT and AST
Echocardiography or abdominal ultrasound as indicated
referral_criteria: Endocrinology for uncontrolled hyperglycemia
Ophthalmology at initial evaluation and every year
Nephrology for deranged renal function
Cardiology for coronary artery disease, heart failure or arrhythmia
level_of_care: Diabetes assessment and monitoring with specialist referral according to complications and control

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Diabetes Mellitus Type 2

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Persistent pulse rate below 50 bpm with syncope, presyncope, dizziness, lethargy or fatigue
Hypotension (systolic BP below 90 mmHg), impaired consciousness or ongoing chest pain
Headache with or without neurological deficit, raising concern for an intracranial event
ECG evidence of complete heart block, sinus-node disease with pauses longer than 3 seconds, or bradycardia below 50 bpm
Pre-existing implanted cardiac device in a symptomatic patient
first_line: Assess pulse and blood pressure and evaluate symptoms and clinical stability
Obtain a 12-lead ECG at PHC/CHC level when available
Review possible reversible causes, including beta-blockers, calcium-channel blockers, digoxin, hypothyroidism, kidney disease and sleep apnoea
For suspected beta-blocker or calcium-channel-blocker overdose, withhold the suspected drug as directed by the workflow
Identify and manage associated conditions such as hyperkalemia according to the ICMR workflow
For unstable patients, arrange urgent treatment and temporary pacemaker insertion; the workflow notes IV dopamine or isoprenaline may be used until temporary pacing can be placed
investigations: Additional testing when indicated: ambulatory ECG, cardiac MRI, implantable loop recorder or electrophysiological study
referral_criteria: Urgent referral for hypotension, impaired consciousness, ongoing chest pain or recurrent/ongoing syncope
Urgent referral for ECG evidence of complete heart block, sinus-node pauses longer than 3 seconds or heart rate below 50 bpm
Refer symptomatic patients with AV-conduction disease, including complete heart block, advanced AV block or Mobitz type II block, for specialist assessment and pacing consideration
Refer symptomatic sinus-node dysfunction with pauses longer than 3 seconds with symptom correlation or awake heart rate below 40/min
Refer unexplained syncope with bundle-branch block or documented transient high-grade AV block when no reversible cause is identified
level_of_care: Initial assessment and basic investigations at PHC/CHC; urgent transfer for unstable or high-risk patients; specialist cardiology assessment for conduction disease, additional testing and permanent pacing decisions

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Bradyarrhythmias in Symptomatic Patients

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Chest pain lasting more than 20 minutes
Chest pain associated with breathlessness, profuse sweating or syncope
Acute left ventricular failure, hypotension, systolic murmur or arrhythmia
first_line: Obtain ECG and troponin at PHC/CHC level
Start the initial treatment listed in the STW: antiplatelet therapy, heparin/LMWH, high-dose statin and metoprolol, as clinically appropriate
Risk-stratify using GRACE or TIMI score
Admit and monitor at district hospital when indicated; very-high/high/intermediate-risk patients require PCI-capable-centre assessment
investigations: Optional: coronary angiography, CT coronary angiography, stress imaging or MRI
referral_criteria: High/intermediate-risk patients: refer to a PCI-capable centre
Low-risk patients: refer to district hospital for further evaluation
Acute LVF, hypotension, systolic murmur or arrhythmia: refer to a PCI-capable centre
Very-high-risk patients: immediate transfer; high-risk patients: same-day transfer; intermediate-risk patients: transfer for PCI within 72 hours
Persistent/recurrent pain, hemodynamic deterioration or new ECG change requires escalation
level_of_care: Initial assessment at PHC/CHC, monitored care at district hospital, and transfer to a PCI-capable tertiary centre according to risk

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Unstable Angina/NSTEMI

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Angina at rest or lasting more than 20 minutes
New-onset effort angina of less than one month
Associated breathlessness, profuse sweating or syncope; assess for acute coronary syndrome
first_line: At PHC/CHC, control angina with metoprolol with or without a dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker; add nitrates if symptoms remain uncontrolled, as specified in the STW
Obtain ECG and assess for Q waves, ST-T changes, bundle branch block or chamber enlargement
Use aspirin and high-intensity statin as specified in the workflow
Address potentiating factors and cardiovascular risk factors; arrange follow-up according to risk
investigations: Other investigations listed: echocardiography, exercise treadmill test, thyroid function test, iron profile, uric acid and HbA1c
Optional: stress radionuclide/echocardiographic imaging and CT coronary angiography
referral_criteria: Refer to STEMI/NSTEMI pathway for rest pain, pain lasting more than 20 minutes, crescendo symptoms or new-onset effort angina
Refer to tertiary centre if angina is uncontrolled on optimal medical therapy
Refer if echocardiography is abnormal, the patient is non-ambulatory, ECG is uninterpretable or exercise stress testing indicates high risk
Refer if symptomatic status changes
level_of_care: Primary/secondary care for initial management and follow-up; tertiary cardiology assessment for uncontrolled symptoms or high-risk findings

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Stable Angina

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Orbital symptoms: periorbital oedema/erythema, displaced globe, double or reduced vision, or ophthalmoplegia
Possible intracranial/meningitis features: fever with headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, altered sensorium or vomiting
Known diabetes, AIDS or immunosuppressive medication use with concern for invasive fungal sinusitis
first_line: For mild/moderate symptoms, address the cause and exacerbating factors
For co-existing allergic rhinitis, use antihistamines and nasal steroid spray as described in the STW
Advise saline nasal wash
The workflow includes steam inhalation and regular physical activity
Consider intranasal steroid spray for 6-8 weeks after discussing risks, benefits and cost
Avoid prolonged topical nasal decongestant use; the STW warns about rebound congestion
investigations: Examine for nasal polyps and assess for allergic rhinitis
Consider skin-prick testing when allergy is suspected
If there is no symptomatic relief, perform nasal endoscopy and consider non-contrast CT of paranasal sinuses
Consider culture-directed antibiotics when purulent nasal discharge is present
referral_criteria: Urgent specialist assessment for orbital or intracranial red flags
Refer/escalate suspected invasive fungal sinusitis
If symptoms do not improve with initial treatment, perform further ENT evaluation including nasal endoscopy and consider CT PNS
Nasal polyps may require endoscopic surgical planning
level_of_care: Initial assessment and treatment with ENT evaluation/escalation for red flags, persistent symptoms or nasal polyps

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for the Management of Chronic Rhinosinusitis

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Unilateral bleeding, nasal obstruction, visual/orbital symptoms or an obvious mass lesion
Altered blood counts or coagulation profile
Possible aneurysmal bleeding, particularly following trauma
first_line: Ensure a patent airway and reduce aspiration risk with appropriate positioning
Restore hemodynamic stability with IV fluids/transfusion as indicated
Apply bidigital nasal compression for 10 minutes in Trotter's position
Identify and control the bleeding point; the STW includes cauterization for a Little's area bleeder
Use anterior nasal packing/epistaxis balloon when required; posterior packing is considered if bleeding is not controlled
Address the identified cause
investigations: Local examination with anterior rhinoscopy/endoscopy to identify the bleeding source
CT with contrast when there is no obvious cause or a benign/malignant lesion is suspected
referral_criteria: Persistent bleeding despite nasal packing
Recurrent profuse bleeding or suspected neoplasia
Altered blood counts/coagulation profile
Suspected aneurysmal bleeding or cases requiring tertiary-level treatment
level_of_care: Initial assessment and non-invasive control; hospital care after packing and tertiary ENT/interventional management for persistent or complicated bleeding

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for the Management of Epistaxis

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

first_line: Confirm CKD and assess stage, progression rate and cause; the STW notes confirmation with repeat tests after 3 months
Identify and treat reversible factors such as hypertension, volume loss, obstruction and infection
Monitor and manage complications including anaemia, bone disease, electrolyte disorders and cardiovascular disease
Advise salt restriction below 5 g/day and protein intake of 0.8 g/kg/day as stated in the workflow
Control blood pressure and diabetes according to the STW, with careful monitoring of medicines and kidney function
At district/tertiary level, investigate the cause, manage complications and discuss renal replacement therapy when indicated
investigations: eGFR using CKD-EPI for adults or Modified Schwartz equation for children
Ultrasound of kidneys and urinary tract
Calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase and albumin
Iron profile: serum iron, TIBC and TSAT
referral_criteria: Refer to a nephrologist if calcium, phosphate, vitamin D, PTH or alkaline phosphatase abnormalities are identified
At eGFR below 30, discuss renal replacement therapy options and preserve veins for possible AV fistula as directed by the workflow
District/tertiary assessment for cause-specific work-up, complications, dialysis access or transplant evaluation
level_of_care: Community/primary monitoring, district-hospital assessment and complication management, and tertiary nephrology care for advanced work-up, renal replacement therapy or transplantation

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD)

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Recurrent UTI or UTI after recent instrumentation
first_line: Make a clinical diagnosis and distinguish uncomplicated from complicated UTI
Assess vital signs, renal-angle tenderness, perineal tenderness and high-risk conditions
Do not routinely send urine culture for uncomplicated UTI; the STW recommends culture when complicated UTI/red flags or other specified indications are present
Select treatment according to UTI type, pregnancy/age group and culture-sensitivity results
Provide symptomatic care as described in the workflow
investigations: Urine dipstick/urinalysis when needed to support diagnosis
Urine culture for complicated/high-risk or non-resolving cases as specified in the STW
Blood culture for selected complicated UTI management
Imaging when indicated, including further imaging for recurrent UTI or abnormal ultrasound
Assess renal function when clinically indicated
referral_criteria: Refer upper UTI/pyelonephritis, infants with UTI and recurrent UTI
Refer bowel-bladder dysfunction and known CAKUT or vesicoureteral reflux
Refer for obstruction/urology services, non-resolving infection or complicated recurrent UTI
Escalate when red-flag signs are present
level_of_care: Primary/secondary care for uncomplicated cases; tertiary/urology care for complicated, obstructive, recurrent or non-resolving cases

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Urinary Tract Infections

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Convulsive seizure lasting more than 5 minutes with loss of consciousness (status epilepticus; medical emergency)
Progressive problems, rapid appearance of new symptoms or recent injury
first_line: Obtain detailed history, preferably from an eyewitness, and distinguish provoked seizures from epilepsy
The STW defines epilepsy treatment consideration as two or more unprovoked seizures; a single seizure may warrant treatment when recurrence risk is high
Use antiepileptic treatment according to the workflow; it advises a broad-spectrum drug, low dose and gradual titration except in status epilepticus
Provide emergency medical care for status epilepticus
Counsel on adherence, side effects, seizure diary, regular sleep and avoiding triggers
investigations: Vitamin D and thyroid function tests where feasible
referral_criteria: Progressive problems or rapid appearance of new symptoms
Recent injury or symptoms after alcohol binge
Status epilepticus after stabilization
Non-response to adequate dose and duration of medication
Serious medication side effects or red-flag signs
level_of_care: Initial diagnosis and treatment at PHC; district hospitals with paediatrician/physician/neurologist for referral cases; specialist follow-up for difficult patients

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for the Management of Epilepsy

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Sudden weakness or numbness, especially on one side
Sudden blurred/double vision or loss of balance/coordination
Sudden severe headache or loss of consciousness
first_line: Assess and manage airway, breathing and circulation
Start cardiac monitoring, maintain oxygen saturation above 94% and establish IV access
Check blood glucose and treat accordingly
Record symptom-onset time/last-known-well time and obtain family contact details
Triage and rapidly transfer to the nearest district hospital with CT or a stroke centre with thrombolysis capability
investigations: Non-contrast brain CT or brain MRI
Bleeding time/clotting time, PT/INR and aPTT
Selected: CTA, echocardiogram, MRI/MRA and Holter monitoring
referral_criteria: All suspected acute stroke requires rapid transfer to a district hospital with CT or a stroke centre with thrombolysis capability
Notify the receiving hospital before transfer where possible
level_of_care: Immediate first response and transfer from initial-care facility to district stroke-capable hospital or tertiary stroke centre; stroke-unit management and rehabilitation thereafter

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for the Management of Stroke

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

first_line: Exclude pregnancy in women of reproductive age after appropriate consent
Take history, examine the patient and use ultrasonography as directed by the workflow
The STW lists supportive/conservative options including tranexamic acid, NSAIDs, progestogens, oral contraceptive pills, LNG-IUS and ormeloxifene according to the clinical pathway
Treat an identified underlying cause, such as thyroid or bleeding disorder, where present
For acute bleeding, follow the STW's urgent management pathway
referral_criteria: Refer to a higher centre if haemoglobin is below 7 g/dL or there is acute ongoing blood loss
Refer if there is no relief or recurrence after treatment
Refer for structural abnormality, atypical hyperplasia/malignancy, adnexal mass or other abnormal findings
Post-menopausal bleeding requires higher-level evaluation in the workflow
level_of_care: Primary-level assessment and treatment, CHC/secondary-level evaluation, and tertiary gynaecology care for persistent bleeding, abnormal findings or procedures

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Heavy Menstrual Bleeding (HMB)

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Blood loss above 500 ml or any bleeding causing derangement of vital parameters
first_line: Call for help and rapidly assess pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate and temperature
Establish two wide-bore IV lines and send blood for grouping/cross-match
Start IV crystalloid as directed by the workflow and provide oxygen
Monitor vital signs, blood loss and input/output frequently
Give oxytocin as specified in the workflow; perform uterine/fundal massage and assess placental completeness
For traumatic bleeding, identify and repair genital-tract tears; for atonic bleeding, follow the uterine-compression and pharmacotherapy pathway
investigations: Assess for coagulation defects when bleeding continues or coagulopathy is suspected
Frequent monitoring of vital signs, blood loss and input/output
referral_criteria: Timely referral to a higher centre when blood transfusion, exploration or surgical-intervention facilities are unavailable
Transport with IV fluids containing oxytocin running and uterine/vaginal tamponade in situ where appropriate and available
Escalate for persistent bleeding, suspected uterine rupture/scar dehiscence or need for surgical intervention
level_of_care: Immediate stabilization at the treating facility with urgent transfer to a higher centre when blood products, exploration or surgery are not available

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Postpartum Haemorrhage

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Clinical fluid accumulation such as pleural effusion or ascites
Mucosal bleeding, liver enlargement above 2 cm, shock, severe bleeding or impaired consciousness
first_line: Suspect dengue with fever and at least two compatible symptoms in a person living in or travelling to a dengue-endemic area
For probable dengue without warning signs, use symptomatic ambulatory management and daily clinical/PCV/platelet monitoring as specified
The STW specifies paracetamol for fever and avoidance of NSAIDs
Assess airway, breathing and circulation; in shock, begin the emergency pathway and arrange urgent referral with monitoring
investigations: Hemoglobin, TLC, DLC, platelet count and PCV
Selected: echocardiography, PCR and CVP monitoring
referral_criteria: Refer for warning signs including cold extremities, restlessness, abdominal pain, reduced urine output, bleeding/hemoconcentration or rising PCV with thrombocytopenia
Shock or severe dengue requires urgent referral to a facility with PICU capability and continuous monitoring
level_of_care: Ambulatory monitoring for dengue without warning signs; hospital/PICU care for warning signs, shock or severe dengue

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for the Management of Dengue Fever

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Dysentery in a child under 1 year or with recent measles/dehydration/systemic illness
Persistent diarrhea with dehydration or serious systemic infection
Poor drinking, repeated vomiting, marked thirst, fever or blood in stools
first_line: Assess general condition, nutritional status and dehydration; classify dehydration using the workflow
Use the appropriate Plan A, B or C management pathway
For some dehydration, the STW specifies ORS in a clinic/daycare setting with reassessment after four hours
Continue age-appropriate feeding and fluids; provide zinc and caregiver education as specified in the workflow
For dysentery, follow the source's treatment and reassessment pathway
investigations: Severe dehydration: CBC and electrolytes; renal function tests and VBG preferred
Suspected cholera: stool hanging-drop test and stool culture preferred
Dysentery not responding to antibiotics: stool culture and stool routine for amoebic trophozoites
Persistent diarrhea: stool and urine microscopy, urine culture and sepsis screen
referral_criteria: Refer to hospital for severe malnutrition/HIV, severe dehydration, significant sodium abnormality, specified dysentery, persistent diarrhea with dehydration or serious systemic infection
Urgent referral for severe dehydration/shock; continue rehydration during transport as described in the STW
level_of_care: Clinic/daycare management for selected dehydration categories; hospital care for severe dehydration, malnutrition, persistent/systemic illness or other referral criteria

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for the Management of Acute Diarrhea

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Life-threatening features: altered sensorium, orthopnea, cyanosis, paradoxical breathing, hypotension or bradycardia

Severe acute asthma: inability to complete sentences, agitation, accessory-muscle use, respiratory rate above 30/min, heart rate above 110/min, pulsus paradoxus above 25 mmHg, silent chest or room-air SpO2 below 92%
first_line: Clinical assessment is the mainstay of diagnosis
Inhaled drugs are the mainstay of pharmacotherapy; treatment initiation depends on symptom frequency in the STW
Educate about adherence, warning signs, triggers, inhaler technique and peak expiratory flow monitoring
Reassess after 3-4 weeks; the workflow notes that a good response supports the diagnosis
Manage acute exacerbations according to severity; severe acute asthma requires admission and oxygen/bronchodilator/steroid treatment as detailed in the source
investigations: Spirometry, if available, to assess airway obstruction and bronchodilator reversibility
Peak expiratory flow monitoring as described in the workflow
Clinical assessment and exclusion of alternative diagnoses
referral_criteria: Immediately refer life-threatening exacerbation to a higher centre with ICU facility
Admit severe acute asthma; refer if there is no improvement
Refer for further diagnostic work-up if the diagnosis is uncertain
level_of_care: Outpatient management for non-severe asthma; hospital admission and higher-centre/ICU referral for severe or life-threatening exacerbations

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for the Management of Asthma

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.

red_flags: Sudden, painful inability to pass urine despite a full bladder (acute emergency)
Phimosis, meatal stenosis, urethral induration, stone or urethral discharge
Complications such as urinary tract infection or acute kidney injury
first_line: Treat acute urinary retention as an emergency
The STW states that no investigation is required before catheterization to relieve symptoms
Attempt gentle urethral catheterization at PHC/CHC using aseptic, atraumatic technique and adequate lubrication
Document the volume of urine drained
If catheterization fails, refer to a urologist; suprapubic cystostomy is an option only where appropriately trained staff are available
The workflow describes keeping the catheter for 1-3 days and subsequent trial without catheter according to the pathway
investigations: After initial relief, desirable tests include CBC, serum glucose, serum creatinine and electrolytes
Urine analysis and urine culture of drained urine
Cystoscopy, CT/MRI, RGU/MCU and urodynamic studies are optional specialist investigations and are not routine
referral_criteria: Refer to a urologist if urethral catheterization fails
Hospitalize patients with significant comorbidities or complications
Refer for specialist assessment when suprapubic catheterization is not safely available or the underlying cause requires specialist management
level_of_care: Initial emergency catheterization at PHC/CHC when trained staff and facilities are available; urology/district/tertiary care for failed catheterization, complications or significant comorbidities

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW): Acute Urinary Retention in Men (AUR)

disclaimer: Structured summary of the cited ICMR workflow. Not a substitute for the complete document or clinical judgement.
